hints.title: Investment Sum Blueprint
hints.text: Select round(sum(tiv_2016), 2) as tiv_2016 where tiv_2015 is in duplicate values subquery and (lat, lon) is in unique coordinate pairs subquery.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT ROUND(SUM(tiv_2016), 2) AS tiv_2016
FROM Insurance
WHERE tiv_2015 IN (
    SELECT tiv_2015
    FROM Insurance
    GROUP BY tiv_2015
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
AND (lat, lon) IN (
    SELECT lat, lon
    FROM Insurance
    GROUP BY lat, lon
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
);
```

variables: N: number of records in Insurance table
complexity.notes: Grouped subqueries and composite tuple checks evaluate in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries or self-joins with Cartesian products scale quadratically on large tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouped aggregation isolates matching keys directly without join explosion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of subqueries with HAVING COUNT(*) conditions and composite tuple filtering.

solutions.approach: PostgreSQL Numeric Rounded Sum with Tuple Filter

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_investments(insurance: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    dup_2015 = insurance[insurance.duplicated(subset=['tiv_2015'], keep=False)]
    unique_loc = insurance.drop_duplicates(subset=['lat', 'lon'], keep=False)
    filtered = insurance[insurance['pid'].isin(dup_2015['pid']) & insurance['pid'].isin(unique_loc['pid'])]
    total = round(filtered['tiv_2016'].sum(), 2)
    return pd.DataFrame({'tiv_2016': [total]})
